__README.purpose: Authoring template for a single blog post that matches the structured article design (hero icon-grid, sticky Table of Contents, numbered sections, feature grids, flow diagram, step list, PRO TIP note, callouts, FAQ).
howToUse: 1. Copy the whole `post` object below into your posts source (one object per blog).
2. Fill every field. Never delete a key you are not using unless it is marked optional; set it to null or [] instead so the renderer stays predictable.
3. `body.sections[]` is an ordered list. Each section renders a coloured number chip + heading, then its `blocks[]` in order.
4. `toc` is generated from `body.sections[]` when `toc.generateFromSections` is true. Only fill `toc.items` to override order/labels/icons.
5. Add as many posts as you want at once - they all follow this same shape, so nothing about the layout drifts.

inlineTextRules.highlight: ==text==  (renders the marker/keyword highlight, e.g. the pink 'Model Context Protocol (MCP)' span)

__README.icons: All `icon` fields take a lucide-react icon name in kebab-case (the project already depends on lucide-react). Examples: zap, bar-chart-3, gauge, lightbulb, clock, check-circle, trending-up, layout-grid, database, server, brain, file-text, star, help-circle, share-2, wrench, map-pin, alert-triangle, list.
__README.accentColors: yellow | purple | pink | green | blue  - used for section number chips, feature icons, step badges, flow-diagram boxes. Sections cycle yellow -> purple -> pink by convention.

callout.title: optional short title, or null
callout.items: optional string[] shown as a mini list, or null

intro.text: Manual reporting is slow, repetitive, and error-prone. By combining Claude AI's advanced reasoning capabilities with the ==Model Context Protocol (MCP)==, you can build a powerful reporting workflow that collects data, analyzes it, and generates actionable insights—automatically.

blocks.text: **Claude** is an advanced AI assistant from Anthropic that excels at understanding, analyzing, and generating human-like text.
**MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an open protocol that allows AI models like Claude to securely connect with external tools, data sources, and systems in a standardized way.
Together, Claude + MCP enable AI to access real-world data, perform complex analysis, and deliver business-ready reports in a consistent, repeatable workflow.

blocks.label: PRO TIP
blocks.text: Use Claude prompts that clearly define:
A weekly sales report that used to take an analyst three hours now runs in under a minute.

blocks.code: Prompt: "Using the attached orders export, write a weekly sales summary. Include revenue vs last week, top 5 products, and one risk to watch."

blocks.text: We went from a Monday-morning scramble to a report waiting in the inbox before anyone logged in.

items: Give Claude the smallest dataset that answers the question - not the whole database.
Version your prompts alongside your code.
Always keep a human review step before a report is shared externally.
Log every run so you can trace how a number was produced.

blocks.title: Watch your data scope
blocks.text: Only expose the MCP resources a workflow actually needs. Broad read access is the most common security mistake.

rows: Google Sheets, Postgres, Shopify Admin API
Official reference servers, custom Node/Python server

items.title: Hallucinated numbers
items.text: Feed structured data and ask Claude to cite the row it used.

items.title: Large datasets
items.text: Pre-aggregate before sending; pass summaries, not raw rows.

items.title: Stale data
items.text: Trigger the workflow on a schedule tied to your data refresh.

items.title: Inconsistent format
items.text: Provide an output template in the prompt every run.

blocks.text: Claude + MCP turns reporting from a recurring chore into a background process. Start with one report, get the prompt and data scope right, then expand.

blocks.alt: Automated report landing in a team inbox
blocks.caption: The finished workflow: raw data in, plain-English report out.

items.q: Do I need to write code to use MCP?
items.a: For off-the-shelf connectors, no. For custom data sources you will need a small MCP server, typically a few dozen lines of Node or Python.

items.q: Is my data sent to Anthropic for training?
items.a: API traffic is not used for training. Still, only expose the data a workflow needs.

items.q: How much does this cost to run?
items.a: Mostly the Claude API tokens per run. A weekly summary over aggregated data is usually a few cents.
